reconcile.note: Gill reads Acts 9:8's report that Paul 'saw no man' as describing his post-vision blindness, not a denial that he had already seen the risen Christ.

discrepancy.note: Cassels reads the Damascus vision as Paul seeing only light, with the identification of Jesus resting on a voice, not sight of a person.

quotes.text: Paul, thus, only sees the light which surrounds the glorified Jesus, but not his own person, and the identification proceeds only from the statement: "I am Jesus whom thou persecutest."
quotes.attr: Walter Richard Cassels (d. 1907), Supernatural Religion, Vol. III (1879), on Acts 9:8 and 1 Corinthians 9:1.

sides.snippet: Saul arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw no one.
sides.verseText: Saul arose from the ground, and when his eyes were opened, he saw no one. They led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.

sides.snippet: Haven't I seen Jesus Christ, our Lord?
sides.verseText: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven't I seen Jesus Christ, our Lord? Aren't you my work in the Lord?
